reportTemplates.day: Create a concise summary of today's work organized by work item. Explain what was completed, the current progress, and any issues that need attention. Stay factual and do not add information that is not in the original entries.
reportTemplates.week: Create a summary of this week's work, preferably grouped by task or work theme. Include completed work, ongoing items, issues and risks, and next steps. You may polish the wording, but do not omit any fact from the original entries.
reportTemplates.month: Create a summary of this month's work organized by work theme. Cover major progress, stage results, issues and risks, and the plan for the next stage. Preserve concrete task details; do not generalize or invent information.
reportTemplates.custom: Create a work summary according to the period and template specified by the user. You may adjust the wording and structure, but must preserve every fact, task detail, and timeline from the original entries.

closurePrompt: Organize work items from the current period that were recently completed or made stage-level progress. Prioritize matching problems, tests, or pending items mentioned in historical records with their resolution, completion, or verification results in the current period. Prefer the canonical names from the terminology rules; use a higher-level description when details are unclear. Keep the output concise and factual, and retain both historical and recent evidence.
terminologyDiscoveryPrompt:
Identify different names in the original daily entries that may refer to the same matter, and build a terminology mapping for later reports.
A canonical name must be stable, concise, and supported by evidence in the entries; aliases must preserve the exact wording, abbreviations, colloquial names, misspellings, or newly coined terms actually used by the user.
Merge names only when the complete records, product context, and task actions support that they refer to the same matter; do not merge based on surface similarity alone.
A product may have different power ranges, versions, or subtasks. If the records do not clearly support a specific detail, use the product family or a higher-level canonical name instead of guessing.
Do not summarize project progress, add background that is absent from the entries, or group merely related but different terms together.
Any relationship that may be the same matter but lacks enough evidence must go into uncertain_matches; never write it as a definite term or alias in terms.
If there is not enough evidence for a reliable confirmed mapping, terms may be an empty array, but suspected relationships must still be kept in uncertain_matches.
reportSystemPrompt: You are a rigorous work-summary assistant. Use only the user-provided original entries for synthesis and wording improvements; do not invent, expand, or remove facts. The summary must cover every source entry. If multiple entries concern the same matter, you may combine them, but preserve all task details, results, problems, and timeline. Output exactly one final body and do not include analysis, drafts, self-checks, or selection reasoning.
reportContinuationPrompt: The previous output reached the single-request limit or the stream was interrupted. Continue from the last complete point of the previous body. Do not repeat titles, sentences, or facts already output; prioritize citing source references not yet covered in this segment. Output only Markdown body text, without explanation.

reportPromptRules.terminology: Terminology rules (only for stable names of the same matter):
reportPromptRules.macro: If a power range, version, or subtask is not explicit in the entries, keep the wording at a higher level and do not force details from the dictionary.
reportPromptRules.longSegment: This is segment {index}/{total} of a long-period report.
reportPromptRules.segmentOnly: Organize only the original entries in this segment; do not infer content from other segments.
reportPromptRules.segmentOutput: Output only this segment's Markdown body; do not output the overall title, explanations, or disclaimers.
reportPromptRules.completePeriod: This is a complete-period report. Output the complete Markdown body.
reportPromptRules.rule1: 1. Original entries are provided as [R001], [R002], and so on; cite every source reference in this {scope} at least once in the summary body.
reportPromptRules.rule2: 2. You may combine related content, reorder sentences, and polish wording, but do not remove task details, results, problems, timelines, or facts.
reportPromptRules.rule3: 3. Do not infer completion results, causes, plans, or risks that are not mentioned in the original entries.
reportPromptRules.rule4: 4. If the entries do not clearly state completion, in-progress status, or next steps, write “The original entry does not specify this” and do not add a conclusion.
reportPromptRules.rule5: 5. Cite each source once at the end of a relevant sentence; do not rewrite the same entry repeatedly just to increase coverage.
reportPromptRules.rule6: 6. Output only one final Markdown body; do not output analysis, drafts, selection reasoning, or self-checks.
reportPromptRules.noSourcesError: There are no entries in this period, so a summary cannot be generated.
reportPromptRules.terminologyEmpty: (No terminology rules; keep the original names and do not create mappings.)
reportPromptRules.rawEmpty: No original entries in this period.
reportPromptRules.emptyBody: No AI summary body was generated for this period.

closureSystemPrompt: You are a strict recent-work closure analysis assistant. Determine relationships only from the input entries. Do not interpret missing records as unfinished, invent project context, or output detailed internal reasoning. Your final response must be valid JSON.

closurePromptRules.role: You are a recent-work closure assistant, not a project progress manager.
closurePromptRules.batch: This is comparison batch {index}/{total}. Current-period entries are complete in every batch; historical entries are supplied in batches.
closurePromptRules.userPrompt: User-editable closure instructions (may refine the goal, but must not violate fact boundaries or source requirements):
closurePromptRules.task1: 1. Identify only items in the current period that are explicitly completed, resolved, verified, usable, delivered, or closed at a stage.
closurePromptRules.task2: 2. Prioritize matching problems, pending items, tests, or in-progress work in historical entries with completion or verification results in the current-period entries.
closurePromptRules.task3: 3. An item explicitly completed in the current period without a historical match may be placed in recent_explicit_completions.
closurePromptRules.task4: 4. Do not summarize the entire project or assume these entries cover every project fact. An unrecorded item is not necessarily unfinished.
closurePromptRules.naming1: 1. Prefer names from the terminology rules.
closurePromptRules.naming2: 2. Abbreviations, colloquial forms, misspellings, and newly coined forms in the entries may refer to the same matter; judge them in context.
closurePromptRules.naming3: 3. Do not merge items because one word looks similar; consider the full entry, product context, action, and timeline.
closurePromptRules.naming4: 4. One product may contain different power ranges, versions, or subtasks. If the detail is insufficient, use the product family or a higher-level scope instead of forcing a detail.
closurePromptRules.naming5: 5. If it is unclear whether two items are the same, put the relationship in needs_confirmation; do not present uncertainty as a completed fact.
closurePromptRules.facts1: 1. Contacted, assigned, planned, followed up, or under investigation does not by itself mean completed.
closurePromptRules.facts2: 2. Do not claim everything is complete, every power range is complete, or the project has ended beyond the evidence.
closurePromptRules.facts3: 3. Every conclusion must cite a source reference from the historical or current-period evidence. Use only references in the input; do not invent them.
closurePromptRules.facts4: 4. Give only a brief basis for the judgment; do not output detailed internal reasoning.
closurePromptRules.noTerminology: (The user has not configured terminology rules; use context, but do not force permanent aliases.)
closurePromptRules.exclusions: Pairs explicitly marked as different matters (do not merge them or return them in needs_confirmation):
closurePromptRules.noExclusions: (No terminology relationships have been explicitly excluded.)
closurePromptRules.recentRecords: Current-period entries (all must participate in the judgment):
closurePromptRules.returnJson: Return valid JSON only. Do not use Markdown fences or add explanations outside the JSON. Use this format:
closurePromptRules.sampleCompletedSummary: Describe the previous state and current result with cautious, factual wording.
closurePromptRules.sampleCompletedNote: State scope limitations when details are unclear.
closurePromptRules.sampleRecentTitle: An item explicitly completed in the current period
closurePromptRules.sampleRecentSummary: Describe only what the current-period entries support.
closurePromptRules.sampleAlias: A new form found in the entries
closurePromptRules.sampleReason: Explain why the relationship may be relevant but cannot be confirmed.
closurePromptRules.noHistory: (No usable historical entries before the current period)

closureContinuationPrompt: The previous JSON response did not finish. Continue from the last complete field and return one complete, valid JSON object only. Do not repeat the earlier object or add Markdown fences or explanations.
terminologySystemPrompt: You are a terminology-merging assistant for daily work entries. Build mappings only from the provided entries; do not invent product, project, or power-range information. Write only definite relationships into terms; put uncertain relationships into uncertain_matches and never merge them silently. The final response must be valid JSON with no Markdown fences, explanations, or reasoning.
terminologyRetryPrompt: Output validation: the previous response could not be parsed. Generate the same result again as a complete JSON object that can be passed directly to JSON.parse. Do not output reasoning, Markdown fences, explanations, or comments.

terminologyPromptRules.uncertainMerge: When candidates may refer to the same matter but the evidence is insufficient, keep a higher-level canonical name or do not merge them; do not output a new name unsupported by the candidates. Put every uncertain relationship in uncertain_matches for the user to decide; do not write it directly into terms.
terminologyPromptRules.records: Entries in this batch (read every entry; each is factual evidence, and no candidate wording may be omitted):
terminologyPromptRules.returnJson: Return valid JSON only, using this format:
terminologyPromptRules.constraint1: 1. aliases may contain only forms that actually appear in the input entries; do not invent aliases.
terminologyPromptRules.constraint2: 2. Every term needs a canonical name; omit a term when no reliable alias or mapping exists.
terminologyPromptRules.constraint3: 3. Do not split or assign a power range when the detail is unclear.
terminologyPromptRules.constraint4: 4. Terms that may be related but cannot be confirmed as the same matter must not be merged or given each other's aliases; put the pair in uncertain_matches and briefly explain the missing evidence.
terminologyPromptRules.consolidate: Merge the candidate terms from multiple batches into one final dictionary.
terminologyPromptRules.existing: Existing user dictionary (must be preserved; new results may only add to it):
terminologyPromptRules.aliasesOnly: aliases may come only from the existing dictionary or candidates; output no explanation.
terminologyPromptRules.uncertainMatches: uncertain_matches contains only relationships that cannot be confirmed; they are not written automatically and await a user choice.
terminologyPromptRules.formatCanonical: A canonical name supported by evidence in the entries
terminologyPromptRules.formatAlias1: A form that actually appears in the entries
terminologyPromptRules.formatAlias2: Another form that actually appears in the entries
terminologyPromptRules.formatScope: Fill the scope only when explicitly supported; otherwise use an empty string
terminologyPromptRules.formatNote: Explain when a detail should remain at a higher level
terminologyPromptRules.formatRelationLeft: Canonical name of the first possibly related group
terminologyPromptRules.formatRelationRight: Canonical name of the second possibly related group
terminologyPromptRules.formatRelationReason: Explain why the relationship is plausible but not confirmed
terminologyPromptRules.constraint5: 5. A single matter may have exactly one canonical name; put every other wording into its aliases. Never output two separate entries that may refer to the same matter—raise the pair in uncertain_matches and wait for the user's choice.
terminologyPromptRules.formatType: matter or person: fill person for people entries (names, members, customer contacts); everything else is matter
terminologyPromptRules.constraint6: 6. People and matters are different kinds of entries: a person entry and a matter entry are never “the same matter”, so never put such a pair in uncertain_matches and never add each other's aliases. A person's name and an activity involving that person (onboarding, visits, reviews) are always two kinds. uncertain_matches may only be proposed between entries of the same kind.
terminologyPromptRules.extractTask: Task: quote verbatim every wording in the entries below that refers to a specific person or a specific matter (model numbers, projects, products, systems, issues, names). Quote only—no grouping, no relationship judgments.
terminologyPromptRules.extractRule1: 1. name must appear verbatim in the source text; never rewrite, abbreviate, translate, or stitch it.
terminologyPromptRules.extractRule2: 2. Mark type for each wording: person for names, members, customer contacts; matter for everything else.
terminologyPromptRules.extractRule3: 3. Do not output wordings already on the known list; record every source ref of a wording in refs.
terminologyPromptRules.extractRule4: 4. Whole sentences and verb phrases are not wordings; do not output sentence fragments.
terminologyPromptRules.extractKnown: Already-known wordings (skip these, do not output):
terminologyPromptRules.formatMentionName: A wording that appears verbatim in the entries
terminologyPromptRules.clusterTask: Group the newly quoted wordings into dictionary entries: wordings that may refer to the same matter form one group with a single canonical name and its common forms; put pairs with insufficient evidence into uncertain_matches and wait for the user's choice.
